stem: An irrigation tank has the expected pH, but its EC is substantially above the normal range. Which conclusion is most defensible?
choices: Expected pH does not explain the high EC, so the EC reading and dissolved-ion load should be verified separately
Expected pH makes the solution acceptable, because a normal acidity reading outweighs changes in conductivity
High EC indicates the substrate is retaining too much water, so irrigation volume should be reduced across the crop first
High EC confirms low alkalinity in the tank, so no additional source-water investigation is needed
rationale: pH and EC answer different questions. A normal pH does not make an abnormal EC irrelevant; the ionic-concentration change needs independent verification and investigation.
